fields.label: Going alone changed the way I travelled.
fields.default: Going alone changed the way I travelled.

fields.label: This trip was not memorable because of one particular sight or one packed itinerary. It mattered bec
fields.default: This trip was not memorable because of one particular sight or one packed itinerary. It mattered because it was my first solo trip. I am naturally social and have never found it difficult to start a conversation, but booking that flight alone was still a different kind of step.

fields.label: Before joining my friends in the Philippines, I gave myself eight days in Thailand: Bangkok, Pattaya
fields.default: Before joining my friends in the Philippines, I gave myself eight days in Thailand: [Bangkok](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Bangkok%2C+Thailand), [Pattaya](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Pattaya%2C+Thailand), Bangkok again, then [Chiang Rai](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Chiang+Rai%2C+Thailand) and [Chiang Mai](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Chiang+Mai%2C+Thailand). I went alone, but the trip kept proving that solo travel does not have to mean being lonely.

groups.label: Familiar places, a new kind of confidence.

fields.label: Familiar places, a new kind of confidence.

fields.label: I already knew Thailand well enough to arrive with a few favourite places in mind. What I did not kn
fields.default: I already knew Thailand well enough to arrive with a few favourite places in mind. What I did not know was how much room a short solo journey could make for chance encounters, local conversations and doing things at exactly my own pace.

fields.default: There was time for the quieter side too.

fields.label: Between flights, scooters, night markets and late conversations, I still found moments that slowed t
fields.default: Between flights, scooters, night markets and late conversations, I still found moments that slowed the whole journey down. Sitting in a temple while monks gathered in front of the Buddha was one of them. It reminded me that Thailand can feel completely different depending on how you choose to move through it.

fields.label: Flying solo did not mean doing everything alone. It meant deciding where to go next, saying yes to c
fields.default: Flying solo did not mean doing everything alone. It meant deciding where to go next, saying yes to conversations and trusting that the unfamiliar would work itself out. Eight days later, I flew from Chiang Mai to meet my friends in the Philippines with more confidence than I had when I arrived.

fields.label: Starting alone, surrounded by familiar faces.

fields.label: I began in Bangkok with three nights in a hotel close to the centre. I was travelling on a budget, b
fields.default: I began in Bangkok with three nights in a hotel close to the centre. I was travelling on a budget, but after a long flight I wanted to give myself a comfortable start: a proper room, a pool and a little space to reset. On the first evening I unexpectedly ran into a good friend from the Netherlands who was travelling through Thailand with his girlfriend. Bangkok already felt a little less lonely.

fields.label: Because I knew the city from earlier trips, I spent my days wandering through familiar streets and f
fields.default: Because I knew the city from earlier trips, I spent my days wandering through familiar streets and finding corners I had missed before. In the evenings, another coincidence appeared: two more friends were also in Thailand, including a former roommate from my earlier months in Thailand and Bali. The plan had been to travel solo, yet the city gave me some of the people I knew best at exactly the right time.

fields.label: One night back in Bangkok, before heading north, I stayed in a hostel and finally felt completely on
fields.default: One night back in Bangkok, before heading north, I stayed in a hostel and finally felt completely on my own in the best way. I spent the day sightseeing, then headed to [Chinatown](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Bangkok+Chinatown) for food. It was a small reset before the part of the trip where I knew nobody at all.

fields.label: A return that felt personal.
fields.default: A return that felt personal.

fields.label: In Pattaya, I visited a friend who had chosen to stay in Thailand after our minor. I checked into Ha
fields.default: In Pattaya, I visited a friend who had chosen to stay in Thailand after our minor. I checked into [Harry’s Hotel](https://www.harryspattaya.com/), a place I already knew from my earlier time in the country. Over three months I had become friendly with the manager and staff, so coming back felt more like seeing people again than simply checking into a hotel.

fields.label: I also met two Dutch travellers who had unexpectedly crossed paths even though they already knew one
fields.default: I also met two Dutch travellers who had unexpectedly crossed paths even though they already knew one another from home. The nights that followed were the kind people summarize with a smile: what happens in Thailand stays in Thailand. The best part was the reminder that travelling alone still leaves plenty of room for shared stories.

groups.label: One small favour turned into a travel friendship.

fields.label: One small favour turned into a travel friendship.
fields.default: One small favour turned into a travel friendship.

fields.label: On the flight to Chiang Rai, I helped a French traveller with his backpack at the airport. The next
fields.default: On the flight to Chiang Rai, I helped a French traveller with his backpack at the airport. The next day, I saw him again while exploring the city’s temples. It was such a random moment that we had to laugh. We spent time together around [Wat Rong Khun](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Wat+Rong+Khun%2C+Chiang+Rai), the White Temple, the [Chiang Rai Clock Tower](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Chiang+Rai+Clock+Tower) and [Wat Rong Suea Ten](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Wat+Rong+Suea+Ten%2C+Chiang+Rai), better known as the Blue Temple.

fields.label: We ate near the Blue Temple, exchanged contacts and later met again at the Chiang Rai Night Bazaar.
fields.default: We ate near the Blue Temple, exchanged contacts and later met again at the [Chiang Rai Night Bazaar](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Chiang+Rai+Night+Bazaar). The night was simple: food, a beer, pool and the local way of going out. It was proof that one friendly moment can change an entire stop on a journey.

groups.label: Choosing local moments over the obvious plan.

fields.label: Choosing local moments over the obvious plan.
fields.default: Choosing local moments over the obvious plan.

fields.label: I finished in Chiang Mai at Mad Monkey. Even in a party hostel, I was more interested in finding the
fields.default: I finished in Chiang Mai at [Mad Monkey](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Mad+Monkey+Chiang+Mai). Even in a party hostel, I was more interested in finding the local rhythm than joining every group plan. A rented scooter gave me the freedom to head out during the day and see places including [Wat Phra Singh](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Wat+Phra+Singh+Woramahawihan), [Wat Chedi Luang](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Wat+Chedi+Luang%2C+Chiang+Mai), [Wat Phra That Doi Suthep](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Wat+Phra+That+Doi+Suthep) and [Baan Tong Luang](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Baan+Tong+Luang+Long+Neck+Karen).

fields.label: The moment that stayed with me most came at Lanna Elephant Care. After a long scooter ride I arrived
fields.default: The moment that stayed with me most came at [Lanna Elephant Care](https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=Lanna+Elephant+Care). After a long scooter ride I arrived near closing time and thought I had missed my chance. Instead, after a long conversation with one of the caretakers, he arranged a small private visit. I could walk beside the elephants, feed them, help with their bath and simply spend time around them. Later, he even took me for food at a local roadside spot. That generosity was as memorable as the elephants themselves.

fields.label: I met the French traveller again in Chiang Mai too, and our conversations continued over drinks and
fields.default: I met the French traveller again in Chiang Mai too, and our conversations continued over drinks and pool. Along the way I met many more people, swapped contacts and made connections I might cross paths with again somewhere else in the world. That is one of the things I love most about travel: the map gets bigger, but so does your circle.
